description: LÃ³rum is a classic Hungarian compendium game played with a 32-card German-suited pack. It consists of a series of diverse 'contracts' or mini-games, traditionally eight in total. Each player takes a turn as the 'declarer' who chooses the round. It is a game of variety, where players must switch from trick-avoidance (negative) to shedding (positive) strategies within a single session. It is deeply rooted in Central European cafe culture.

history.origins: Developed from the 19th-century 'Quodlibet' and 'King' families of games, tailored for the 32-card Hungarian Tell deck.
timeline: 1880s: Compendium games using Tell cards become popular in Budapest.
1920s: The 'LÃ³rum' name and specific 8-round sequence are standardized.
Present: A beloved social game often played in Hungarian families and university clubs.
2004: Digitized for online card game archives.
history.cultural: Commonly played for chips (krajcÃ¡r) or matchsticks in a social competitive setting.
history.evolution: The game's 'Suta' (Train) round became so popular that it is sometimes played as a standalone game, but in LÃ³rum, it remains just one part of the journey.

setup.deck: 32 cards (Hearts, Bells, Leaves, Acorns). Ace is high.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 8 cards. The dealer rotation ensures everyone gets to lead each contract type once.

rules.objective: Score the fewest penalty points (or most chips) across the full rotation of contracts.
rules.gameplay: Eight contracts played in sequence: 1. **No Tricks**: Avoid winning any tricks. 2. **No Hearts**: Avoid capturing Heart cards. 3. **No Red King (FelsÃ¶)**: Avoid the King of Hearts (The 'Old Man'). 4. **No Last Trick**: Avoid the 8th trick of the round. 5. **Suta (The Train)**: Players must shed cards by building sequences. First to finish wins. 6. **Quart**: A variation of the 'Seven-Up' sequence building. 7. **Everything Negative**: No tricks, no hearts, no red king combined. 8. **Goulash**: A special high-scoring final round.
keyRules: Standard trick-taking for avoidance rounds: Must follow suit. No trumps unless specified.
Each contract played 4 times before rotating to next dealer.
Suta is a shedding round (positive scoring).
Lowest cumulative score after all contracts wins.

strategy.basic: Keep the Seven of Hearts until the very end of the 'No Hearts' round. It is your only escape from taking a large point penalty if someone leads the suit when you are low.
strategy.intermediate: 'Old Man' Trapping: In the 'No Red King' round, if you hold the Red King, you MUST try to empty your hand of other Hearts as quickly as possible. Once void, you can dump the Red King on any other heart lead safely.
strategy.advanced: Suta Sequencing: In the shedding round, don't just play your cards because you can. Hold onto a card that 'blocks' your opponent's sequence if you know they have the card immediately following yours.
tips: Track the rotation of chips. If you are the declarer for the 'Suta' round, play aggressively, as common rules allow the winner to take 2x the standard payout.
In 'Everything Negative', focus solely on avoiding the Red King; it is worth more points than five standard hearts combined.
